Currency Act
(CHAPTER 69)
Currency
(Denominations and Characteristics of Coins) (No. 4)
Notification 2014
Pursuant to section 17(5) of the Currency Act, it is hereby notified for general information that the denominations and characteristics of the coins to be issued on 8 January 2015 by the Monetary Authority of Singapore are as shown in the Schedule.

Milled and bearing the words “MONETARY AUTHORITY OF SINGAPORE” and a lion symbol.
In the centre is the Singapore Arms with the year‑date “2015” below it, and the word “SINGAPORE” in the 4 official languages around the circumference of the coins. The position of the mintmark is at 5 o’clock for all the proof coins.
Inspired by Chinese calligraphy, the goat in the centre is symbolised by the appropriate Chinese character of the “Heavenly Stems and Earthly Branches” to enhance the characteristics of the animal and the oriental cultural flavour. The peony, a traditional Chinese symbol of blessings and festive cheer, is incorporated into the body of the goat and ushers in the Lunar New Year. The 2 Chinese characters signifying the “Year of the Goat” are at the upper centre of the design. The denomination of the coin in figures is below the design and the weight in troy oz/grams and fineness are at the lower circumference for all the coins except for the $2 cupro‑nickel coin.
